I'm a little confused by all the positive reviews of Bay Glen Animal Hospital. Based on our experience,  I tend to believe reviewers, here and on Yelp, who feel their pets suffered from sloppy care. They don't have the ability to keep patients overnight and have a workaround of sending animals to VCA for overnight monitoring and treatment. This creates extra stress for sick animals, work for their families who are expected to bring them back and forth daily between facilities, an increased potential for mistakes due to lack of continuity of care, and diffused responsibility between the vets should anything go wrong. It also makes it cost a LOT more because you pay a premium for any services at an overnight emergency vet. I wonder how many pet parents get surprised by this arrangement at the last minute when an animal needs overnight care since it isn't obvious from the website and who would expect things to be done this way? Anyway, for me, just this setup would be a deal breaker even if everything else was great which it wasn't.

In general, I didn't get an especially positive impression of anyone who worked at Bay Glen, including Dr. Delgado. When we picked Spot up to take him for overnight monitoring at the VCA following his surgery, the tech told us his catheter wasn't inserted well and not to be surprised if it came out during the trip. I'm not sure why they'd feel okay sending an animal out that way but we made sure that the VCA staff knew it needed to be adjusted. Apparently, they didn't do that, resulting in extra blood coming out in his urine all night and speculation from the VCA vet about a need to perform more surgery or to euthanize this young cat. Luckily we were able to switch to a different, better vet for a second opinion and better prognosis.

In addition, the Bay Glen office isn't clean. When we were there bright and early (because the VCA was closing at 8:00 AM and Spot had to be out of there and moved to Bay Glen), there was a strong smell of old feces. Since they don't keep animals overnight and we were one of the first customers through the door, this means they had left it dirty overnight. When we were back later in the day (schlepping the poor cat back to VCA for overnight monitoring following surgery), there was a strong chemical air freshener, presumably covering up the animal waste smell.

There are plenty of good vets in this area. I'd encourage you to find one.
